data.title: Creative Technologist
data.description:
About Black Forest Labs

We’re the team building the foundational layer for visual intelligence: multimodal models trained jointly on images, video, audio, and action to see, generate, and understand the world.

Our founding team pioneered latent diffusion and Stable Diffusion, the breakthroughs that made generative AI accessible to millions. With FLUX, we're pushing into generative media at scale, machines that act in the physical world, and emerging applications in computer use.

Our FLUX models top public benchmarks and run in production in some of the world's biggest platforms. We're a small, fast growing research lab competing with the largest companies in the world. From our labs in Freiburg to San Francisco, we're building what comes next.

Why This Role

Our models need someone who knows them inside out — not just what they can do today, but what nobody has tried yet. You'll create the work that makes people realize what's possible with generative media: original pieces, experiments, and creative assets that set the standard for what FLUX can do, and show it to the world.

What You'll Work On

  • Build end-to-end production workflows that push FLUX to its limits — experiments, visual explorations, and pieces tailored to brand, agency, and entertainment use cases that show what's possible before anyone else figures it out.

  • Test and explore models, endpoints, and features that are still in development — you're the one figuring out what they can actually do, and turning that into new insights for image, video generation and more

  • Create and maintain a library of demo boards, templates, and pipelines that make the product's value obvious in live pitches. Partner with Sales and FDEs on discovery and demo prep, and document what works so it scales across the team.

  • Support customer enablement - help define what's feasible for custom projects, fine-tuning, and creative workflows.

  • Work with DevRel, Product, Marketing and Growth to turn experiments into shareable, reproducible examples and insights.

What We're Looking For

  • 3+ years in creative technology, digital art, or experimental media.

  • You use generative AI for image and video every day, deeply and practically — enough to know intuitively where it breaks down and where it delivers.

  • A portfolio that demonstrates strong taste, solid craft, and versatility across mediums and tools.

  • Background in brand, agency, or film/VFX work — you understand the real process behind shipping professional creative.

  • You move easily through the FLUX ecosystem and the tools around it, from ComfyUI to AI Toolkit and beyond.

  • Deep understanding of generative AI, agents, and diffusion models.

  • Working knowledge of Python for scripting and rapid prototyping.

Nice to Have

  • Active presence in the creative AI community (X, Discord, YouTube) — you're already someone people follow for generative AI work.

  • Experience creating content that got real traction in the AI/creative space.

  • Experience supporting Sales or GTM teams with creative assets and technical feasibility assessments.

How We Work Together

We’re a distributed team with real offices that people actually use. You’ll be based in Freiburg or SF and work from the office at least 2 days a week.

Everything we do is grounded in four values:

  • Obsessed. We are a frontier research lab. The science has to be right, the understanding deep, the product beautiful.

  • Low Ego. The work speaks. The best idea wins, no matter who said it. Credit is shared. Nobody is above any task.

  • Bold. We take the ambitious bet. We ship, we do not wait for conditions to be perfect.

  • Kind. People over politics. We treat each other with genuine warmth. Agency without empathy creates chaos.

If this sounds like work you’d enjoy, we’d love to hear from you.

Compensation : $220K - $320K + equity, depending on profile

  • Fixes for partner friction and weak performance, by finding root causes, weighing quick fixes against long term commercial impact, and growing referral volume, quality and conversion. You'll give internal teams actionable feedback to improve processes and remove barriers to partner success.

  • Compelling partner pitches and value propositions, adapted for commercial, operational and technical audiences and backed by data, while balancing priorities between partners and internal teams and keeping working rhythms predictable and trusted.

What you'll bring

  • Commercial acumen: you know partnerships should generate merchant leads and revenue, and you can balance partner satisfaction with Mollie's performance targets.

  • Comfort with outreach, industry events and networking to sign new partners.

  • Teamwork and project management skills: you collaborate, share partner materials and ideas, and work independently after onboarding.

Grow your way
At Mollie, growth is personal. We believe everyone should have the chance to develop their skills, explore new challenges and shape their career on their own terms.

No matter if you're aiming for promotion, exploring a different career path or building new skills, you'll be supported with the tools, trust and opportunities to grow your way.

data.title: Senior Produktionscontroller (m/w/d)
data.description:
Ihre neue Herausforderung als Senior Produktionscontroller (m/w/d)

Sie kennen die Zahlen hinter einer Produktion und möchten künftig nicht nur analysieren, was passiert ist, sondern gemeinsam mit Ihrem Team mitgestalten, was als Nächstes kommt? Dann könnte diese Position gut zu Ihnen passen.

Als erfahrene:r Produktionscontroller (m/w/d) übernehmen Sie die fachliche Verantwortung für ein kleines, erfahrenes Team und bleiben gleichzeitig nah am operativen Tagesgeschäft. Ihr fachliches Know-how ist bei uns ebenso gefragt wie Ihre Fähigkeit, Aufgaben zu strukturieren, Prioritäten zu setzen und die unterschiedlichen Stärken im Team zusammenzubringen.

Unser Produktionscontrolling ist eng mit den Abläufen unserer Produktionsstandorte verzahnt. SAP bildet dabei das Herzstück unserer täglichen Arbeit und die zentrale Datenbasis für Abrechnung, Kalkulation und Analyse. Gemeinsam mit Ihrem Team möchten wir unsere Prozesse kontinuierlich weiterentwickeln und die Möglichkeiten von Digitalisierung und Automatisierung noch stärker nutzen. Sie schauen gemeinsam, wo neue Lösungen einen echten Mehrwert schaffen, Abläufe erleichtern und mehr Raum für die analytischen Aufgaben des Controllings ermöglichen.

Folgende Aufgaben erwarten Sie an unserem Standort in Hamburg-Wilhelmsburg:

  • Sie übernehmen die fachliche Führung und Weiterentwicklung unseres kleinen Teams im Produktionscontrolling, koordinieren Aufgaben und sorgen gemeinsam für verlässliche Abläufe im Tagesgeschäft.

  • Sie verantworten die Abrechnung unserer Produktionsaufträge für die Abpackbetriebe der CAFEA-Gruppe, analysieren die Ergebnisse und arbeiten dabei eng mit unseren Produktionsstandorten zusammen.

  • Sie behalten Herstellkosten, Bestände sowie die Auftrags- und Kostenstellenrechnung im Blick und stellen gemeinsam mit den relevanten Schnittstellen eine verlässliche Datenbasis in SAP sicher.

  • Sie verantworten Kalkulationsläufe sowie relevante Sonderauswertungen und interne Kalkulationen und leiten aus den Ergebnissen die passenden Fragestellungen und Handlungsbedarfe ab.

  • Gemeinsam mit Ihrem Team entwickeln Sie Prozesse, Auswertungen und unser Berichtswesen weiter und nutzen Digitalisierung und Automatisierung dort, wo sie die tägliche Arbeit sinnvoll unterstützen.

  • Darüber hinaus bringen Sie Ihr Know-How in standortübergreifende CAFEA-Projekte ein und arbeiten mit unterschiedlichen Fachbereichen und internationalen Kolleginnen und Kollegen zusammen.

Was Sie mitbringen

Sie sind fachlich gerne mittendrin, können gleichzeitig den Überblick behalten und haben Freude daran, Menschen, Zahlen und Prozesse zusammenzubringen? Dann passen Sie möglicherweise ziemlich gut zu uns.

Ob Ihr beruflicher Weg über ein betriebswirtschaftliches Studium, eine kaufmännische Ausbildung mit entsprechender Weiterbildung oder über mehrjährige praktische Erfahrung geführt hat, ist für uns dabei weniger entscheidend. Wichtig ist uns, dass Sie über fundierte Erfahrung im Controlling, idealerweise im Produktions- oder Werksumfeld, verfügen und betriebswirtschaftliche Zusammenhänge sicher beurteilen können.

Sie haben bereits erste Verantwortung für andere übernommen, beispielsweise als fachliche Führungskraft, Stellvertretung, Projektleitung oder in einem kleinen Team? Perfekt. Sie müssen bei uns keine langjährige Führungskarriere mitbringen. Viel wichtiger ist, dass Sie gerne Verantwortung übernehmen, Orientierung geben, zuhören und Ihr Wissen mit anderen teilen.

Unser Angebot

  • Digitalisierung gemeinsam gestalten: Wir möchten die Möglichkeiten neuer Technologien künftig noch stärker für unser Produktionscontrolling nutzen. Dabei setzen wir auf Lösungen, die zu unseren Prozessen und vor allem zu den Menschen passen, die täglich mit ihnen arbeiten.

  • Bei uns erwartet Sie nicht nur ein sicherer Arbeitsplatz, sondern auch eine langfristige Perspektive in einem international tätigen Familienunternehmen. Sie erhalten eine attraktive Vergütung, ergänzt durch Weihnachtsgeld, Urlaubsgeld sowie regelmäßige Gehaltsanpassungen.

  • Wir möchten, dass Sie sich bei uns langfristig wohlfühlen und Ihre Arbeit flexibel gestalten können. Deshalb bieten wir Ihnen moderne Arbeitsbedingungen mit Gleitzeit, flexiblen Arbeitszeiten und der Möglichkeit, bis zu zwei Tage pro Woche mobil zu arbeiten.

  • Gemeinsam wachsen: Wir fördern Ihre persönliche und fachliche Weiterentwicklung durch individuelle Weiterbildungsmöglichkeiten und externe Qualifizierungsangebote. Bei uns erhalten Sie Gestaltungsspielraum und die Möglichkeit, Verantwortung für spannende Projekte und Produkte zu übernehmen.

  • Auch außerhalb des Arbeitsplatzes möchten wir etwas zurückgeben: Sie profitieren von Zuschüssen zur betrieblichen Altersvorsorge, JobRad, vermögenswirksamen Leistungen, Deutschlandticket sowie vergünstigten Sport- und Gesundheitsangeboten über machtfit.

  • Karriere mit Geschmack: Sie erhalten monatliche Freikontingente, damit Sie auch nach der Arbeit erstklassigen Kaffee, Cappuccino und Trinkschokoladen genießen können.

  • Damit nicht nur unsere Produkte überzeugen, sondern auch Ihr Arbeitsalltag angenehm bleibt, wird in unserer betriebseigenen Kantine täglich frisch gekocht.

  • Dank unserer Kooperation mit dem Fürstenberg Institut erhalten Sie und Ihre Familienangehörigen Zugang zu professioneller und vertraulicher Beratung – bei beruflichen, privaten oder familiären Themen.

  • Unsere Mitarbeitenden liegen uns am Herzen. Neben den vielfältigen Angeboten gehören auch kleine Aufmerksamkeiten zu Geburtstagen, Ostern, Nikolaus oder Weihnachten bei uns einfach dazu.

Dürfen wir uns kurz vorstellen?

Familiär. International. Langfristig.

Besondere Qualität entsteht, wenn Tradition und Moderne miteinander harmonieren. 

Wir gehen respektvoll, offen und hilfsbereit miteinander um und geben jeden Tag unser Bestes, um erstklassige Kaffee-Spezialitäten zu produzieren.

Bei der DEK arbeiten Sie in einem internationalen Umfeld und spüren zugleich die Vorteile eines inhabergeführten Familienunternehmens.

data.description:
The company

Small businesses move fast. Opportunities often don’t wait, and cash flow pressures can appear overnight. To keep going, and growing, SMEs need finance that’s as flexible and responsive as they are.

That's why we built iwoca. Our smart technology, data science and five-star customer service ensures business owners can act with the speed, confidence and control they need, exactly when it's needed.

Our ultimate mission is to support one million SMEs in their defining moments, creating lasting impact for the communities and economies they drive.

We’re looking for a Financial Crime Analyst

If you’re curious, analytical and enjoy getting into the details, this could be the role for you. You’ll dive into suspicious activity, help protect small businesses from fraud and financial crime, and play a key part in keeping our processes sharp and secure. We're looking for candidates based in either London or Leeds.

The role
iwoca's Financial Crime Analysts protect our customers and our business from fraud. You'll become an expert in how fraudsters target small businesses and card products, helping our business credit card grow safely while keeping the experience smooth for genuine customers.

You'll investigate suspicious applications, accounts and card activity, owning the process from first alert to final decision. Working closely with our Credit Cards and Operations teams, you'll spot new fraud patterns early to help strengthen our controls. From time to time, you'll also support our core lending business with fraud cases on our Flexi-Loan, giving you a wider view of financial crime across iwoca.

Your mission will be:

  • Investigating cases flagged as a potential fraud or AML risk. Including CIFAS flags, facial biometric anomalies, device based anomalies, signs of document tampering and more.

  • Screening PEP, sanction and adverse media matches.

  • Taking ownership of customer verification on a case by case basis and deciding what information is required to reduce the risk of fraud and money laundering.

  • Monitoring account activity and transactions, investigating anything unusual and raising unusual activity where needed.

  • Identifying opportunities to improve our processes and implement changes which will make us more efficient

  • Working closely with our Account Managers, Credit Analyst and Broker teams to maintain our high fraud prevention standards while ensuring a fast and slick service.

The requirements

We look for people who are smart, humble, motivated and who are always looking to improve.

Ideally, you’ll have:

  • At least 1 years’ experience within a financial crime related role

  • Good knowledge of fraud and financial crime

  • Brilliant communication skills and experience delivering constructive and candid feedback

  • A confident and enthusiastic attitude that works well in a regularly changing and fast-paced environment

  • A pragmatic, risk-based approach to case investigation

  • An analytical mindset with a practical approach to problem solving, sometimes we need to make decisions with limited information

Whilst we welcome applications from all qualified candidates, please note that this particular position does not offer visa sponsorship. Candidates must be eligible to work in the UK independently.

The salary

Our base salary range in Leeds is £30,000 - £35,000 and our base salary range in London is £35,000 - £40,000. We want to pay all of our employees fairly, so that’s why we regularly benchmark salaries based on market rates and to recognise your increasing value to our business.

The culture

At iwoca, we prioritise a culture of learning, growth, and support, and invest in the development of our team members. We value thought and skill diversity, and encourage people to explore new areas of interest, adopt better tools – including AI – and apply sound judgement so our products and decisions improve over time.

The offices

We put a lot of effort into making iwoca a great place to work:

  • Offices in London, Leeds, Berlin, and Frankfurt with plenty of drinks and snacks.

  • Events and community-led groups, including running groups, padel, and monthly ping-pong and pool competitions.

The benefits

  • Flexible working hours.

  • Medical insurance from Vitality, including discounted gym membership.

  • A choice between a dedicated dental plan or a health cash plan that reimburses everyday medical expenses.

  • A private GP service (separate from Vitality) for you, your partner, and your dependents.

  • 25 days’ holiday per year, an extra day off for your birthday, the option to buy or sell an additional five days of annual leave, and unlimited unpaid leave.

  • A one-month, fully paid sabbatical after four years.

  • Instant access to external counselling and therapy sessions for team members that need emotional or mental health support.

  • 3% Pension contributions on total earnings.

  • An employee equity incentive scheme.

  • Generous parental leave and a nursery tax benefit scheme to help you save money.

  • Electric car scheme and cycle to work scheme.

  • Two company retreats a year: we’ve been to France, Italy, Spain, and further afield.

And to make sure we all keep learning, we offer:

data.title: Staff Backend Engineer - Ledger Platform
data.description:
Staff Backend Engineer - Ledger Platform

Hybrid in London, UK

We’re looking for a Staff Backend Engineer to join the Ledger Platform team.

You'll design and build iwoca's new ledger platform – the distributed system that records every movement of money, starting with the business credit card and moving on to loans.

The company

Small businesses move fast. Opportunities often don’t wait, and cash flow pressures can appear overnight. To keep going, and growing, SMEs need finance that’s as flexible and responsive as they are.

That's why we built iwoca. Our smart technology, data science and five-star customer service ensures business owners can act with the speed, confidence and control they need, exactly when it's needed.

We’ve already cleared the way for 100,000 businesses with more than £4 billion in funding. Our passionate team is driven to help even more SMEs succeed, through access to better finance and other services that make running a business easier. Our ultimate mission is to support one million SMEs in their defining moments, creating lasting impact for the communities and economies they drive.

The team

The Ledger Platform team is rebuilding all of iwoca’s ledgers as one platform, starting with the ledger for the business credit card. Every card payment, loan repayment, and payout will end up there. Finance, Accounting, and Capital Markets rely on that record, so it has to be right every time.

The team is small – a principal engineer who leads it, another staff engineer, another engineer, and you. It works closely with the product teams that build on its ledgers, and with Finance.

The role

You'll lead projects from design to production, and decide with product what the team builds and how. With the principal engineer, you’ll set the platform’s technical direction, from service boundaries to the APIs and event streams other teams build on. Most of the platform is still to be built, and you’ll own part of it yourself. It’s a hands-on individual contributor role with high ownership and no line management.

Every payment a small business makes with iwoca crosses several services and network hops before it reaches the ledger, and any of them can fail. You'll build services that record each one exactly once, with no single point of failure, safe timeouts and retries, and graceful degradation when a dependency is down. When something breaks in production, you'll fix it so it doesn't break again.

You’ll learn iwoca’s financial products in depth, so you can challenge requirements and explain technical trade-offs to Finance. When the answer isn’t obvious, you’ll scope and prototype, and use domain modelling to find the simple design behind a complicated problem. You’ll influence which parts of a problem need solving now, which can wait, and which aren’t worth solving at all.

Live project examples:

  • New ledgers. Building the ledgers for Flexi-Loan and iwocaPay.

  • Account migration. Moving existing loan accounts onto the new ledgers with zero downtime and no data lost.

  • Credit card ledger. Building new features for the credit card ledger, from real-time card holds to daily interest and monthly statements.

  • Reconciliation and journals. Reconciling the ledger with banks, payment providers, and the card scheme, and producing the accounting journals Finance relies on.

  • Funding facilities. Recording how loans move between iwoca’s funding facilities.

The requirements

Essential:

  • Distributed systems. You’ve built and run fault-tolerant services in production, and handled the hard parts: durable communication between services, idempotency, transactional correctness, and partial failure.

  • Backend engineering. You have deep expertise in at least one object-oriented language. You’ve written and run backend services in it.

  • Databases. You’ve worked in depth with relational databases, ideally PostgreSQL, and solved data integrity, concurrency, and performance problems in them.

  • Ownership. You’ve led large projects across several engineers or teams, end to end, and helped other engineers grow through design and code reviews.

  • Testing. You’ve tested for edge cases and failures as carefully as you designed for them.

  • AI leverage. You’ve built agentic workflows, or used AI to scale your engineering output beyond what you could deliver alone, at work or in your own projects. You judge when to use it and when not to, and you check its output before it reaches production.

  • Communication. You write and speak clearly, directly, and concisely. You adapt technical detail to your audience.

Bonus:

  • Financial systems. You’ve built ledgers, billing, or payment systems, including the audit trails and reconciliation that prove they’re correct.

  • High volume. You’ve worked at a company where the volume of data or transactions shaped how you designed systems.

data.description:
About Volta

Volta is the category-defining, fully vertically integrated AI infrastructure platform – from capital to clusters to software, under a founder-led enterprise. Our mission is The Utility of Compute™: AI infrastructure as dependable and available as electricity, for every organization that needs it. Launched with a $10B strategic partnership with one of the leading frontier AI labs, a Series A led by Andreessen Horowitz, and a $5B AI Infrastructure Fund, Volta is building the infrastructure layer of the AI era from the ground up. We are 100+ people across London, Palo Alto, and New York, with rapid growth expectations to hundreds.

About The Role

As a Technical Program Manager for GPU and Data Center Deployments, you will own end-to-end program delivery for bringing data center infrastructure and AI clusters online. You will operate in a highly ambiguous environment, coordinating across construction, infrastructure, networking, systems engineering, procurement, and operations — driving execution from planning through operational handoff.

 

This is an ownership role. You will be expected to move programs forward with incomplete information, surface and resolve gaps before they become blockers, and hold multiple workstreams accountable across time zones and organizational boundaries. The best candidates bring deep experience at the intersection of data center construction handover and AI/GPU hardware deployment. You know how construction sequences impact infrastructure readiness, how ICT and CDU work intersect, and how to drive multi-threaded bring-up programs spanning hardware, networking, power, and cooling.

 

What You'll Do

Program Delivery & Execution

  • Own end-to-end delivery of GPU cluster activations and data center infrastructure programs, from initial strategic planning through operational handoff.

  • Drive multi-threaded bring-up programs spanning hardware, networking, power, and cooling — owning plans, dependencies, and critical paths.

  • Coordinate cross-functional teams responsible for construction, infrastructure, network, hardware, ICT, commissioning, and operations, including vendor and contractor partners.

  • Anticipate downstream impacts of technical sequencing decisions on capacity, schedule, and cluster performance; identify and resolve blockers before they surface.

  • Manage and hold accountable vendors, integration contractors, and third-party service providers across the full deployment lifecycle.

  • Partner with engineering to improve cluster turn-up reliability, repeatability, and automation — reducing time-to-serve for new capacity.

  • Support network operations and end-to-end physical and logical bring-up, including on-site deployment, rack cabling, and coordination with engineering teams.

  • Maintain momentum through changing requirements, tight timelines, and cross-time-zone execution.

Stakeholder & Executive Communication

  • Influence senior executive and c-suite strategic approaches.

  • Deliver crisp executive-level program status briefings covering schedule health, risks, key decisions, and escalation paths across a broad portfolio of concurrent programs.

  • Translate complex technical requirements — from highly detailed customer RFPs, integration specs, and architecture documents — into actionable plans for engineering, finance, and marketing stakeholders.

  • Serve as the primary cross-functional point of contact between engineering, operations, customers, and leadership; code-switch fluently between deeply technical and business-facing audiences.

  • Interface with chip and hardware providers to derisk onboarding to new platforms across compute, networking, and cooling stacks.

  • Facilitate alignment across stakeholders at all levels — from network engineers to C-suite — with confidence, clarity, and no ego.

Program Infrastructure & Process

  • Build and operationalize program mechanisms — roadmaps, milestones, risk registers, RACI matrices, decision logs, and deployment runbooks — that make delivery predictable at scale.

  • Establish and maintain a single source of truth for all active programs using tools such as Smartsheet, Confluence, Jira, and Notion.

  • Identify bottlenecks and systemic gaps, then drive durable fixes across tooling, process, and partner interfaces.

  • Develop scalable playbooks and governance frameworks that create accountability without creating overhead as Volta's deployment footprint grows rapidly.

  • Champion automation and digital workflows to eliminate manual effort across the program lifecycle.

 

What You'll Bring

Required

  • 5+ years of experience delivering complex data center physical infrastructure programs or large-scale GPU/AI cluster deployments in fast-moving environments.

  • Demonstrated experience bridging construction handover and cluster deployment — candidates who are network-only or construction-only will not be a fit.

  • Hands-on GPU deployment experience, including:

  • GPU cluster deployment and activation (NVIDIA infrastructure preferred)

  • Full-stack secure AI factory deployment across compute, networking, storage, and security layers

  • Ability to read, interpret, and operationalize highly technical customer and vendor specifications

  • Strong understanding of AI/GPU infrastructure including power density, cooling (CDU/DLC), networking, and deployment sequencing.

  • Familiarity with how construction, low-voltage, and commissioning activities affect deployment readiness and sequencing.

  • Proven ability to lead through influence — you don't own the execution teams, but you are accountable for delivery outcomes.

  • Proven ability to manage vendor and contractor relationships, including understanding schedule and reputational risks.

  • Ability to develop and present executive-level program status, risk summaries, and key decisions to senior leadership and cross-functional stakeholders.

  • Excellent communication and stakeholder alignment skills — able to ensure teams at all levels understand priorities and dependencies.

  • Relentlessly resourceful: you thrive in ambiguous, fast-paced environments and drive execution beyond your defined scope without being directed to do so.

  • Startup or scale-up experience alongside enterprise pedigree is strongly preferred — candidates who have operated at both ends of that spectrum understand the range of environments this role will demand.

Preferred

  • Degree in a hard science, engineering, or a demonstrated track record of technical depth in comparable work.

  • Experience delivering programs across multiple concurrent sites or regions, including EMEA, with staggered milestones.

  • Experience managing long-lead procurement processes and hardware supply chain constraints that affect deployment timelines.

  • Background at a Fortune 100 infrastructure company (NVIDIA, Intel, Dell, Cisco, Verizon, AT&T) combined with startup or scale-up experience.

  • Experience managing BPO or contract labor pools during large-scale hardware deployment phases.

  • Automation-first mindset with experience identifying and implementing process improvements at scale.

  • DCD, PMP, CDCPM, CDCMP, CDCP, or comparable certification(s).

 

Who You Are

  • You have operated in highly ambiguous, fast-moving environments and know how to prioritize ruthlessly without losing sight of the long-term picture.

  • You have startup instincts — you fill gaps, take initiative, and drive execution beyond your defined scope before anyone asks you to.

  • You have enough confidence to hold the room and none of the ego that slows the work down.

  • You are not a 9-to-5 operator. Global infrastructure programs run across time zones — you know how to chase the sun.

  • You have built the business case, secured buy-in from technical stakeholders, and presented to executive decision-makers who pushed back hard.

  • You bring a strong execution mindset with the ability to balance speed, quality, and risk — and you make decisions with data, not assumptions.

  • You are interested in and thoughtful about the impact of AI infrastructure on the world.

What We Offer

At Volta, we believe people do their best work when they feel supported, trusted and able to grow. We're building a company where you can make an impact, keep a healthy balance between work and life, and build a career you're proud of.
As a global team, we do our best to provide great benefits wherever you're based. While some benefits vary by country due to local regulations, we believe looking after our people is simply the right thing to do.

About Volta

We are 100+ people across London, Palo Alto, and New York, with rapid growth expectations to hundreds.

About the role

Volta builds and operates large scale GPU compute infrastructure for frontier AI customers. Growing this fast produces a long tail of manual internal work: invoices retyped into banking portals, expense reports chased by hand, spreadsheets reconciled every month, accounts provisioned ticket by ticket. Each task is small. Together they cost the company real time, and they multiply with every new sit and every new hire.

This role removes that work permanently. You sit with the person who owns a process, understand what it actually does, then build the integration that runs it against banking and accounting systems, Microsoft Graph / Office, Slack, Jira and Confluence, and the HR and identity stack. Most of the answer is well built API code with sound authentication, error handling, escalation, audibility and observability. Some of it uses models, for classification, extraction, or matching, where that is the right tool rather than the fashionable one. Knowing the difference is a large part of the job.

Much of this work lands inside the financial reporting path, and Volta is building toward SOX compliance alongside its existing ISO 27001 and SOC 2 obligations. An automation that touches invoices, payments, or reconciliation becomes part of the control environment the moment it goes live. That sets the bar: changes are reviewed, tested, and traceable, access is least privilege and segregated, every run leaves an audit trail an external auditor can follow, and nobody moves code into production by hand. You build to that standard from the first commit rather than retrofitting it under deadline.

Regulation shapes the work in a second way. Volta is headquartered in the UK and operates across the EU, so anything you build with AI in it sits under the EU AI Act as well as UK and EU data protection law. Automation that touches hiring, performance, or other employment decisions carries the heaviest obligations, and the line between a helpful classifier and a regulated decision system is easy to cross without noticing. You are expected to recognize where that line runs, keep a person in the loop where the law requires one, document what you deploy, and bring Legal and Security in early rather than after the build.

You sit inside Corporate IT at a fast-growing AI-forward company, which owns the tooling, accounts, and API access you build on, and which gives you engineers next to you for design discussion and code review rather than leaving you to mark your own homework. Security Engineering advises on access and compliance. The first internal customer is the accounting and finance team. After that the scope is the whole company: finance, IT, People, delivery, product, and the engineering teams for their own internal overhead. Very little here is customer facing. Initially, you are the only person doing this work full time, so you prioritize hard, ship small, and build things that keep running without you next to them.

What You Will Be Doing

  • Automate finance operations first: ingest received invoices into banking and bookkeeping systems, classify and match them, and close the loop on the exceptions

  • Work directly with process owners across finance, IT, People, and delivery: take a described workflow and turn it into a specified, testable automation

  • Work as part of Corporate IT: review their changes, have yours reviewed, and keep automation aligned with how the underlying systems are administered

  • Build and run integrations against internal systems, including Microsoft Graph, Slack, Atlassian, banking platforms, and HR and identity tooling

  • Own authentication and credentials for those integrations: OAuth flows, service principals, scoped tokens, secret rotation

  • Build every finance touching automation to withstand audit: version controlled and peer reviewed changes, automated deployment with no manual production edits, least privilege service identities, segregation of duties preserved rather than automated away, and retained evidence of what ran, when, and on whose authority

  • Work with Finance and Security Engineering on control design, so an automation replaces a manual control with a stronger automated one instead of quietly removing it

  • Apply models where they earn their place, for document extraction, classification, or matching, and use conventional code everywhere else. Keep a human decision point where a control requires one

  • Build agentic automations where a single scripted path will not hold: an agent that picks up a case, calls the tools it needs across Microsoft Graph, Slack, Atlassian and the finance stack, and stops at a human approval gate before anything with money or access impact. You define the tool surface, the permitted scope, and the blast radius, rather than handing a model a broad credential and watching what happens.

  • Keep AI use inside its regulatory boundaries: automatically classify use cases correctly under the

  • EU AI Act, apply transparency and human oversight where required, document deployed systems, and escalate anything touching employment decisions to Legal before it is built

  • Instrument what you build so failures surface immediately and the state of any run is visible without reading logs

  • Maintain what you deploy, including the unglamorous part where an upstream API changes and the process still has to run on Monday

  • Set the patterns, repositories, and review practices that keep internal automation maintainable and auditable as more of it accumulates

  • Push back when a process should be simplified or deleted instead of automated

What You Bring

  • Production software development held to the standard of an engineering team, not scripting attached to an operational role

  • Fluency across more than one software ecosystem. Internal systems arrive in whatever language, runtime, and SDK their vendor picked, and you are expected to work in what the problem needs rather than bending every problem toward one stack. Python and Go come up often here, neither is a requirement

  • Deep practical work with third party APIs: pagination, rate limits, idempotency, retries, webhooks, and how an integration behaves when the far end is having a bad day

  • Real command of authentication mechanisms, including OAuth 2.0, OIDC, service accounts, and API key and secret management

  • Disciplined engineering practice that produces an audit trail as a by-product: source control, code review, automated testing, controlled deployment, and clear separation between who builds a change and who releases it

  • Hands on experience building with LLMs, including tool use and structured extraction, plus the judgment to recognize when a model is the wrong answer

  • Hands on work with agentic patterns: tool and function calling, MCP or equivalent tool interfaces, state and retry handling across multi step runs, and testing agent behavior against realistic cases before it touches a production system.

  • Working awareness of the rules governing AI and automated decision making in a workplace context, at the level of knowing which use cases need legal review before a line of code is written

  • Ability to sit with a subject matter expert, understand a business process well enough to implement it correctly, and translate it without needing them to specify the solution

  • A track record of building reliable, secure, auditable systems rather than demos that work once

  • Comfort as the only engineer on a problem: choosing what to build next and owning the outcome

Nice to Have

  • Delivering AI systems under the EU AI Act: risk classification, technical documentation, transparency and human oversight obligations

  • Building or operating systems in SOX scope: IT general controls, change management, segregation of duties, and producing evidence for external audit

  • Finance systems experience: accounts payable, expense management, bank reconciliation, ERP integration

  • Microsoft Graph, Slack, Atlassian, or identity platform APIs at more than a tutorial level

  • Workflow orchestration tooling and the failure modes that come with it

  • Document processing and information extraction at production quality

  • A company scaling past 100 people, where processes are new and requirements move

What We Offer

At Volta, we believe people do their best work when they feel supported, trusted and able to grow. We're building a company where you can make an impact, keep a healthy balance between work and life, and build a career you're proud of.

data.description:
Our Global Structure


Deliveroo is now part of DoorDash, bringing together teams with even greater reach, scale, and ambition. Depending on your role, you may collaborate with teammates, systems, and leaders across DoorDash and Wolt. Together, we're unlocking new possibilities as one global team.

Join us in our mission to transform the way people shop and eat, where impact, innovation and growth drive everything we do. Our Global Engineering teams tackle complex technical challenges across a global, three-sided marketplace, building and scaling systems that serve millions of customers, riders and partners every day.

We're looking for a Senior Machine Learning Engineer to join our London office as part of a Global DoorDash Engineering team (working hybrid, 3 days in the office).

This role sits in our Consumer Org, where you'll work on recommendation problems with direct, measurable impact on how customers discover relevant content. You'll collaborate with experienced scientists and engineers across DoorDash, Deliveroo and Wolt, learning from multiple recommendation systems while helping shape the next generation of the experience.

What You'll Be Doing

  • Design, develop and improve recommendation, ranking and retrieval models that surface relevant restaurants, dishes, items and content to customers.
  • Own applied ML problems end to end: frame the problem, analyze data, develop models, define offline evaluation, run experiments and monitor production performance.
  • Develop methods that balance relevance with product and customer needs, such as diversity, availability, business constraints and changing user intent.
  • Collaborate closely with Software Engineers, ML Engineers, Product Managers and Analysts to turn scientific insights into reliable customer-facing products.
  • Evaluate and apply state-of-the-art ML methods where they meaningfully improve recommendation quality, robustness or efficiency.
  • Contribute to a high bar for applied-science practice through technical reviews, knowledge sharing and thoughtful experimentation.

What You'll Need to Thrive

  • You have substantial hands-on experience applying machine learning to real-world problems and a track record of bringing models from development into production; a PhD with relevant applied research experience is equally welcome.
  • You have experience with recommendation systems, ranking, retrieval, personalisation, or closely related ML problems.

data.title: Senior Software Architect
data.description:
Senior Software Architect – Computer Vision & Tracking

 

Shape the technology behind some of the biggest moments in world sport.

From goal-line technology and semi-automated offside in football to electronic line calling in tennis and automated ball-strike systems in baseball, Hawk-Eye's tracking technology plays a critical role in elite sport around the world.

 

We're looking for an exceptional Senior Software Architect to shape the future of this technology.

This is a unique opportunity to combine software architecture leadership with deep computer vision expertise, influencing the technical direction of products used across football, baseball, tennis, American football, ice hockey, cricket, basketball and rugby.

 

Working across our Tracking and Automated Officiating (T&AO) value stream, you'll influence an engineering organisation of more than 100 people, setting architectural direction, driving innovation and helping solve some of the most complex tracking challenges in sport.

 

This is a senior, hands-on individual contributor role. You'll have significant technical influence while remaining close to the engineering, research and problem-solving that make our technology possible.

 

What you'll do

 

Set the architectural direction

  • Lead software architecture across our tracking, automated officiating and data delivery products.

  • Define how new tracking challenges are approached and ensure consistency across products and sports.

  • Shape our shared frameworks, libraries and core technology, making pragmatic decisions about reuse, scalability and performance.

  • Represent Tracking within engineering architecture forums across Hawk-Eye and Sony Sports.

 

Drive computer vision innovation

  • Act as the senior technical authority for computer vision across Hawk-Eye's tracking technology.

  • Set the direction for camera calibration, ball tracking, skeletal tracking and machine learning integration.

  • Research and evaluate emerging technologies, building prototypes to turn promising ideas into practical solutions.

  • Help resolve the most complex technical challenges and ensure our technology continues to evolve.

 

Champion modern engineering

  • Lead the adoption of AI-powered development tools, including agentic coding frameworks, LLM orchestration and automated code generation.

  • Establish practical standards for using these technologies within our large C++ and Python codebases.

  • Explore opportunities in generative AI and synthetic data to accelerate research and improve tracking capabilities.

 

Develop engineering capability

  • Coach and mentor Squad Tech Leads and emerging architects.

  • Share expertise through technical talks, tutorials and knowledge-sharing sessions.

  • Support recruitment and technical assessment for computer vision and machine learning roles.

  • Help ensure our ML training and synthetic data infrastructure is operationally sustainable.

 

What we're looking for

We're looking for someone with exceptional expertise in multi-camera computer vision, combined with the software engineering and architectural experience to influence technology at scale.

 

Computer vision expertise

  • Deep knowledge of multi-camera calibration, including intrinsics, extrinsics, distortion models, anti-wobble and bundle adjustment.

  • Strong understanding of triangulation, 3D ball tracking, pose estimation and skeletal tracking.

  • Experience with continuous-time modelling and inverse kinematics.

 

Software engineering and architecture

  • Expert cross-platform C++ development across Windows and Linux, x86 and ARM.

  • Strong experience with CMake, performance profiling and optimisation.

  • Proven ability to architect complex, high-performance systems across multiple teams and products.

 

Machine learning and infrastructure

  • Experience with GPU inference technologies such as TensorRT and Triton.

  • Strong knowledge of ML frameworks and pipelines, including PyTorch and ONNX.

  • Experience deploying tracking systems across AWS, on-premise infrastructure and edge devices.

  • Understanding of generative AI and synthetic data generation.

 

Modern engineering practices

  • Hands-on experience with AI coding agents and LLM orchestration.

  • An interest in applying emerging AI technologies to accelerate algorithm research, development and refactoring.

 

The person we're looking for

You'll be a confident technical leader who can influence decisions across multiple engineering teams, communicate complex ideas clearly and make pragmatic architectural choices.

You'll be comfortable working with senior stakeholders and external technology partners, including Sony, NVIDIA and AWS, as well as sports leagues and federations.

Just as importantly, you'll know when to challenge existing approaches, balance technical ambition with commercial realities and make clear recommendations on priorities, risks and investment.

 

Why join Hawk-Eye?

Our technology is trusted across some of the world's biggest sporting competitions. You'll have the opportunity to:

  • Shape the architecture behind internationally deployed sports technology.

  • Influence the technical direction of more than 100 engineers.

  • Work on fascinating challenges across computer vision, 3D tracking, machine learning and real-time processing.

  • Explore and introduce emerging technologies, including AI-powered engineering tools.

  • Collaborate with world-leading technology partners and sporting organisations.

  • Remain hands-on while operating at the highest level of technical influence.

 

If you're passionate about computer vision, thrive on complex engineering challenges and want to help shape the future of technology in sport, we'd love to hear from you.

data.title: Montu Pharmacy Assessment Centre
data.description:
Ready to start or take the next step in your pharmacy career?

At Montu, we are doing things differently, and that includes how we recruit.

We are growing, and we are looking for enthusiastic, hardworking and patient-focused individuals to join our pharmacy team in Winnersh Triangle.

Whether you are looking to take your first step into healthcare, explore a new career in pharmacy or bring your existing pharmacy experience to a rapidly growing organisation, we would love to meet you.

We are hosting a Pharmacy Assessment Centre on Saturday 5th December, giving you the opportunity to experience a different approach to recruitment, demonstrate your skills and learn more about what it is like to work at Montu.

You do not need previous pharmacy experience for all of our opportunities. For our entry-level positions, what matters most is your attitude, willingness to learn and genuine commitment to making a difference to patients.

Our pharmacy is busy. Really busy. It is a lively, energetic environment where things move quickly, teamwork is essential and no two days are quite the same. If you enjoy being on your feet, working alongside others and being part of a team where everyone has a role to play, you could feel right at home.

Behind every prescription we process is a patient relying on us to get things right. Whether you are packing medication, dispensing prescriptions or completing final accuracy checks, your contribution matters.

Opportunities Available

We are recruiting across several positions within our pharmacy team, with opportunities for both experienced pharmacy professionals and individuals looking to enter the industry.

Pharmacy Assistant

An excellent entry point into the pharmacy sector, with no previous pharmacy experience required.

You will support the day-to-day operations of our busy pharmacy, including preparing orders, packing medication, supporting stock management and helping ensure prescriptions are processed accurately and efficiently.

We are looking for individuals who are organised, reliable, comfortable with repetitive tasks and enjoy working in a hands-on, fast-paced environment.

Trainee Pharmacy Dispenser

Looking to develop a career in pharmacy? This could be your opportunity.

No previous dispensing experience is required. You will receive training and support as you develop the knowledge and practical skills needed to work within our dispensing team.

You will learn about prescription processing, medication handling, accuracy, pharmacy procedures and the importance of maintaining high standards of patient safety.

Pharmacy Dispenser

For individuals with an existing dispensing qualification and experience working within a pharmacy environment.

You will support the safe and accurate dispensing of prescriptions, working closely with pharmacists, technicians and the wider pharmacy team.

You will need excellent attention to detail, a strong understanding of pharmacy procedures and the ability to maintain accuracy while managing high prescription volumes.

Accuracy Checking Dispenser

We are looking for qualified and experienced Accuracy Checking Dispensers who can help maintain the high standards of accuracy and patient safety expected within our pharmacy.

You will undertake accuracy checking duties within the scope of your qualification, training and authorisation, supporting the efficient processing of prescriptions and working collaboratively with the wider team.

Accuracy Checking Technician (ACT)

For qualified Pharmacy Technicians with an accredited accuracy checking qualification and current GPhC registration.

You will play an important role in maintaining dispensing accuracy, supporting pharmacy operations and ensuring our processes meet the required professional and regulatory standards.

You will bring confidence, attention to detail and the ability to work effectively in a high-volume dispensing environment.

What Is Our Pharmacy Assessment Centre?

We know that traditional interviews do not always give people the best opportunity to demonstrate what they can do.

That is why we are taking a slightly different approach.

Our Pharmacy Assessment Centre is designed to be an engaging, practical and interactive experience where you can demonstrate your abilities, meet members of the Montu team and gain a better understanding of our working environment.

You can expect a combination of practical and team-based activities designed to assess skills relevant to working within our pharmacy, including:

  • Attention to detail and accuracy

  • Literacy and the ability to follow written instructions

  • Working effectively with others

  • Organisation and the ability to follow processes

  • Speed and efficiency without compromising accuracy

  • Communication and problem-solving

We are not expecting everyone to arrive with pharmacy knowledge, particularly those applying for our entry-level opportunities.

We are interested in how you approach tasks, how you work with others and whether you have the right attitude to succeed in our environment.

What happens after the assessment centre?

Candidates who successfully complete the assessment centre will be invited to attend a further on-site interview at Montu on a later date.

Please note that attendance at the assessment centre does not guarantee an interview or offer of employment.

What Are We Looking For?

We are looking for people who genuinely want to be part of a team making a difference.

Our ideal candidates will be:

  • Patient-focused: You understand that the work you do has a direct impact on the people relying on our service.

  • Detail-oriented: Accuracy matters, particularly when working with medication.

  • Comfortable in a busy environment: You enjoy an energetic workplace and can remain focused when things get hectic.

  • Reliable and hardworking: You take pride in doing your job well and supporting the people around you.

  • Team players: You understand that pharmacy operations depend on people working together.

  • Adaptable: You are comfortable learning new processes and responding to change.

  • Eager to learn: Whether you are new to pharmacy or already experienced, you are motivated to develop your skills.

You do not need to be the loudest person in the room or have years of experience to succeed here.

What matters is your work ethic, your attention to detail and your commitment to doing things properly.

About Montu

Montu is a leading medical cannabis company working to improve access to cannabis-based medicines for patients across the UK.

Through our specialist clinical services and pharmacy operations, we support patients receiving prescribed cannabis-based medicines for a range of eligible medical conditions.

Our multidisciplinary teams bring together clinicians, pharmacists, pharmacy technicians, dispensers and operational colleagues, all working towards the same goal: delivering safe, effective and patient-centred care.

We are a rapidly growing organisation, and our pharmacy is at the heart of what we do.

Every prescription represents a patient who is depending on us. From the moment a prescription reaches our pharmacy to the moment medication is dispatched, every member of our team plays an important role in that patient journey.

We are proud to be helping shape an evolving area of healthcare, and we want people who are excited to be part of that journey.

Why Join Montu?

Joining Montu means becoming part of a growing organisation where your work has purpose and your contribution makes a difference.

We offer:

  • Competitive salaries dependent on the position, qualifications and experience

  • Opportunities for training and professional development

  • Career progression within our growing pharmacy operations

  • A supportive and collaborative team environment

  • The opportunity to gain experience within a specialist area of healthcare

  • The chance to be part of a growing business helping improve patient access to prescribed medication

Further information about the benefits applicable to each role will be provided during the recruitment process.

Ready to Join Us?

Assessment Centre: Saturday 5th December

Location: Winnersh Triangle, Berkshire

If you are looking for an opportunity to begin a career in pharmacy, develop your existing skills or take the next step within a growing healthcare organisation, we would love to hear from you.

Apply now to be considered for a place at our Pharmacy Assessment Centre.

Following an initial review of applications, shortlisted candidates will receive further information about the assessment centre, including timings, location details and what to expect on the day.

data.title: Eco Toxicologist Risk Assessment Consultant
data.description:
About 3E:

3E is a mission-driven company dedicated to creating a safer and more sustainable world. We offer award-winning regulatory intelligence and AI solutions to help organizations protect people and products. With over 35 years of experience and a global presence, we empower our customers with innovative compliance solutions. 

You will get to work at a company that combines startup agility with the stability of an industry leader. Partner with enterprise customers and global experts to advance environmental safety and solve complex data science challenges.

Join us and make an impact!

About Yordas

3E, the leading global provider of expert-led AI compliance solutions for chemical and workplace safety, product stewardship, and sustainable supply chains, recently acquired Yordas Group, a leading international provider of scientific consulting and regulatory content services across chemical management, sustainability, and regulatory compliance.

Headquartered in Lancaster, UK, with operations in Germany, Canada, Turkey, and Japan, Yordas serves global brands through its Scientific Services, Regulatory Intelligence, Product Compliance, and Hazard Communication offerings.

About the Role

Understanding the potential impact of chemicals on human health and the environment is essential to helping businesses develop safer products and meet evolving regulatory requirements. At Yordas, recently acquired by 3E, you'll have the opportunity to apply your scientific expertise to complex regulatory challenges while contributing to the growth of our risk assessment services.

We're looking for an (Eco)toxicologist / Risk Assessment Expert to join our expanding regulatory and scientific consultancy business. In this role, you'll help clients navigate chemical safety requirements across REACH, Biocidal Products Regulation (BPR), and Cosmetics Regulations, providing the scientific insight needed to assess hazards, evaluate exposure, and manage risk.

You'll collaborate with toxicologists, human health experts, chemists, external research partners, and clients to deliver high-quality scientific assessments and regulatory guidance. Beyond the technical work, you'll have the opportunity to contribute to the development of our risk assessment services across chemicals, biocides, cosmetics, medical devices, and food contact materials.

This opportunity is well suited to someone who enjoys translating complex science into practical recommendations, working across disciplines, and applying their expertise to a diverse range of regulatory and product safety challenges.

What You'll Do

  • Evaluate chemical and product safety: Conduct toxicological and ecotoxicological assessments to evaluate potential risks to human health and the environment under REACH, BPR, and Cosmetics Regulations.

  • Apply scientific modeling to real-world challenges: Perform quantitative exposure and risk assessments using tools such as CHESAR and other simulation models to evaluate human and environmental exposure.

  • Translate scientific data into regulatory insight: Review and interpret toxicological studies, hazard information, regulatory guidance, and applicable legislation to develop scientifically sound risk assessments.

  • Deliver high-quality regulatory reports: Prepare chemical safety reports that clearly communicate assessment methodologies, scientific findings, and risk characterization to support regulatory compliance.

  • Coordinate external scientific studies: Commission and oversee physicochemical and environmental fate studies conducted by Contract Research Organizations (CROs), ensuring technical quality and timely delivery.

  • Collaborate across scientific disciplines: Work closely with toxicologists, chemists, human health specialists, and other technical experts to develop comprehensive assessments and client deliverables.

  • Provide trusted technical guidance: Communicate scientific findings, support technical positions on behalf of clients, and engage with regulatory authorities and other stakeholders on chemical safety matters.

Purpose of the Role

TrustFlight’s Operations department delivers a high volume of aviation safety training, consultancy, and compliance services to clients globally. As the business scales, the administrative and coordination burden across scheduling, travel, contracting, and client communications has grown significantly.

This role exists to identify, design, and implement digital and AI-powered solutions that automate and streamline the operational workflows underpinning consultant scheduling, travel logistics, contractor management, and client-facing communications — including course joining instructions, certificates, course materials, and Microsoft Teams setup.

The AI & Digital Solutions Engineer will act as the bridge between operational need and technology capability, transforming manual, repetitive processes into scalable, intelligent workflows that free the wider team to focus on high-value delivery. Whilst Operations is the primary focus, the role will also extend AI and automation capability into Business Development and Product, supporting pipeline workflows, proposal generation, and product feedback processes as the function matures.

Scope & Decision-Making Authority

  • Design, build, and deploy automation solutions for agreed operational workflows using AI and no-code/low-code tooling, within a structured support framework during the initial onboarding period.

  • Select and recommend appropriate tools and platforms for workflow automation, within agreed budget parameters and subject to IT governance sign-off.

  • Propose and pilot new digital solutions with line manager oversight, progressing toward greater autonomy as experience and confidence develop.

  • Escalate to Operations Director for significant new vendor contracts, material changes to client-facing communications, or solutions that touch personal or sensitive data.

  • Cross-functional coordination with Training Delivery, Consulting, Client Success, Business Development, and Product teams to gather requirements and implement agreed solutions.

  • Scope covers Operations as the primary function, with cross-functional remit extending to Business Development and Product from day one.

Key Relationships

Internal

  • Operations Director — regular check-in on priorities, solution sign-off, and strategic alignment.

  • Operations Coordinators, Admins & Consultants — day-to-day requirements gathering, testing, and adoption support for new workflows.

  • IT & Engineering — technical governance, data security review, and integration support where required.

  • Senior Leadership Team — periodic reporting on operational efficiency gains and automation ROI.

  • Business Development Team — automation of proposal generation, CRM workflows, and pipeline reporting.

  • Product Team — digital tooling support for product feedback loops, release communications, and internal reporting.

External

  • Training & Consultancy Clients — automated and semi-automated communications for joining instructions, certificates, course materials, and Teams invitations.

  • Contractors & Freelance Consultants — digital onboarding, contracting, scheduling notifications, and engagement management.

  • Software & Platform Vendors — procurement, configuration, and ongoing management of automation and scheduling tools.

Key Responsibilities

  • Audit and map current operational workflows — including consultant scheduling, travel booking, contractor contracting, and client communications — to identify automation and AI opportunities.

  • Design and build end-to-end digital workflows using AI tools, automation platforms, and scheduling systems to reduce manual effort across the Operations team.

  • Implement intelligent scheduling solutions for consultant time allocation, ensuring visibility of availability, conflict resolution, and automated notifications to all parties.

  • Automate the full client communication lifecycle for training and consultancy engagements, including generation and dispatch of joining instructions, course materials, Teams meeting invitations, and post-course certificates.

  • Build and maintain a digital contractor management workflow covering sourcing triggers, contract generation, engagement tracking, and payment milestone coordination.

  • Own the technology stack for Operations automation — evaluating tools, managing licences, and ensuring solutions remain fit for purpose as the business evolves.

  • Champion adoption of new digital workflows across the Operations team, providing training, documentation, and ongoing support.

  • Monitor solution performance, identify failure points, and continuously improve automations to increase reliability and coverage.

  • Support the Business Development team with AI-assisted proposal workflows, CRM automation, and pipeline visibility tooling to accelerate the sales cycle.

  • Collaborate with the Product team to design and implement digital solutions that streamline product feedback collection, internal reporting, and release communication processes.

Key Metrics for Success

  • Within 90 days: Full audit of operational workflows completed and an automation roadmap agreed with the Operations Director.

  • Within 6 months: At least 3 core workflows automated (e.g. consultant scheduling notifications, client joining instructions, contractor contract generation), with measurable reduction in manual processing time of ≥40%.

  • Within 12 months: End-to-end automation coverage across scheduling, travel coordination triggers, client communications, and contractor onboarding, delivering a quantified saving of ≥60 hours/week for the Operations team.

  • Client communication error rate (wrong materials, missed invites, late certificates) reduced to <1% of engagements.

  • Deliver at least one agreed automation solution for each of Business Development and Product within the first 12 months.

AI & Digital Competency

data.title: Engineering Manager
data.description:
TrustFlight builds software that aviation operators around the world rely on to keep flying safe, for an international customer base with an unusually varied set of problems. This role exists to build and sustain a high-performing team of six to eight engineers: coaching each individual, holding a consistent standard of performance, and owning the process, testing, tooling and infrastructure the team depends on. It is a people and systems leadership role rather than a technical leadership one. Product and the technical leads decide what gets built and how; the Engineering Manager owns the conditions that allow them to build it well and quickly. The postholder is one of four Engineering Managers in a Product, Design and Engineering department of around 40 to 50 people, which is growing and maturing quickly. There is considerable scope here to shape how engineering works across it. 


Key Responsibilities:

  • Raise the performance bar with every hire and every promotion. Treat coaching as a core duty of the role, and upskilling as a standing remit: develop engineers through regular 1:1s, direct feedback, stretch assignments and explicit development plans, and grow technical leads as well as individual contributors. 

  • Manage performance fairly and decisively. Set explicit expectations, recognise strong work, raise problems early and allow runway to respond, and address sustained underperformance promptly. 

  • Act as the chief unblocker for the team across tooling, infrastructure, testing and process, and own the team's infrastructure-as-code estate. Identify the genuine constraints on throughput, including code review latency, slow or flaky tests, handoffs, approval gates and unreliable environments. Remove them, ensure the team can build, test, deploy, observe and recover quickly and safely, and evidence the improvement in flow metrics. 

  • Own testing standards and the consistency of quality across the team, including the definition of “tested”, the criteria that gate a release, and the management of coverage and test flakiness. Quality should not vary according to who wrote the code. 

  • Architect cross-team developer tooling and drive consolidation of the technology estate, jointly with peer Engineering Managers and the Director of Engineering. Build the case for moving from a varied stack onto fewer, better-supported technologies. Establish paved roads and automated guardrails that teams adopt on merit, and sequence the change so that it strengthens delivery. 

  • Work with the technical leads to maintain an accurate and current picture of technical debt, quality and process constraints. Translate it into risks and opportunities the Product Manager can prioritise, so that the balance between product output and technical excellence is a deliberate decision. 

  • Lead the team's adoption of AI-assisted development. Set the standards for where and how AI is used, ensure AI-generated code is understood and accountable to a named engineer, guard against data, licensing and security risk, and maintain an evidence-based view of its effect on the team. 

  • Help establish consistent engineering practice across TrustFlight with the other Engineering Managers. No shared approach to levelling, calibration, feedback and hiring yet exists, and building one is part of this role, so that an engineer's experience does not depend on which manager they report to. 

Required Qualifications & Experience: 

  • At least three years' experience as a dedicated people manager of software engineers, including senior engineers and, ideally, technical leads. 

  • A software engineering background sufficient to contribute credibly in a design review, challenge an architectural decision on its merits, and distinguish a team that feels fast from one that is fast. The postholder will not act as the team's technical lead and will not be assessed on code they write. 

  • Current, practical familiarity with infrastructure-as-code, CI/CD and automated testing, covering Terraform, Pulumi or equivalent, containerised deployment and a major cloud platform, sufficient to own the estate, set standards and review the work. 

  • A track record of raising and holding a quality bar across a team: testing strategy, review standards, and the discipline to keep them consistent as the team and the codebase change. 

  • Demonstrable experience of improving how a team works, supported by evidence of the resulting difference. 

  • Direct experience of performance management, including at least one case of successfully improving, or fairly exiting, an underperformer. 

Desirable Skills & Experience 

  • Practical experience of agentic development setups, using tools such as Claude Code, Codex or Cursor, introduced at team or organisation level along with the governance around them. 

  • Experience building or operating auditable agent orchestration systems. A strong advantage, though not a requirement. 

  • A track record of putting AI workflows into real use, and of helping ship AI features in production applications. 

  • An understanding that this field is changing quickly, with the adaptability to keep pace and the credibility to bring a team along on that journey. 

  • Experience leading, or contributing materially to, a technology-stack consolidation across multiple teams. 

  • Experience raising standards across a heterogeneous or inherited technology estate without mandating uniformity. 

  • Experience in a regulated, safety-critical or externally audited software environment, such as aviation, medical, defence or financial services. Valuable, though not a requirement. 

AI & Digital Competency 

TrustFlight is an AI-first organisation. Every role is expected to actively engage with AI tools and digital ways of working to drive efficiency, quality, and innovation. 

 

Tier 3 — AI Builder 

Develops and integrates AI-powered solutions 

Builds, fine-tunes, or integrates AI/ML models and pipelines. Establishes evaluation frameworks for AI systems. Ensures responsible AI practices (fairness, transparency, data governance). Contributes to TrustFlight’s AI strategy. 

 

Role-Specific AI & Digital Skills: 

  • Set and maintain the team's standards for AI-assisted development, covering which tools are approved, where they may and may not be used, and how their output is reviewed. 

  • Ensure AI-generated code entering the codebase is understood and accountable to a named engineer, and that review capacity scales with the volume AI produces. 

  • Apply AI to strengthen testing and documentation, ensuring that AI-written tests validate the requirement and do not simply confirm the behaviour of the implementation. 

  • Establish guardrails against the specific risks of AI-assisted engineering: leakage of customer or regulated data into model context, licensing contamination, and plausible but incorrect code in safety-relevant paths. 

AI Development & Growth 

  • Complete TrustFlight's AI fluency onboarding within the first 30 days. 

  • Dedicate time each month to evaluating emerging AI development tooling and agentic workflows, and pilot promising tools in a controlled way. 

  • Share findings with the Engineering Manager group and the wider engineering team, including negative results. 

  • Contribute to TrustFlight's engineering-wide standards for AI-assisted development, and to the evidence base available to customers and auditors. 

Competencies & Behaviours:

  • People Leadership — Raises the bar with every hire and promotion; coaches deliberately and develops leaders as well as engineers; creates the conditions for people to do their best work. 

  • Fairness and Consistency — Applies the same bar and the same care to everyone; makes reasoning visible; is trusted by engineers and by peers in calibration. 

  • Systems Thinking — Treats delivery problems as problems with the system rather than with the people; identifies the constraint before asking for more effort; takes obstacles off other people's desks and measures success by the team's output. 

  • Technical Judgement — Sufficient depth to ask the right question, weigh a trade-off, and defer to the technical leads when appropriate. 

  • High Standards in a Safety Domain — Holds a consistent quality bar and does not allow defects to pass down the line; recognises that operators' safety cases depend on this software. 

Working Arrangements: 

Working Hours: 

40 hours per week 

Work Pattern:

Hybrid. London-based, with a minimum of two days per week in the London office and the remainder flexible. 

Travel Requirements:

Occasional travel to other TrustFlight locations and to team or company events. Not a regular requirement of the role. 

On-Call / Shift Work:

Not part of the on-call rota. Accountable for the team’s on-call practice being sustainable and fairly shared. 

Special Conditions:

Right to work in the UK. Background screening as required for access to customer and regulated data, including ability to obtain CTC.

Au sein de l'équipe Administration & Finance France, le/la Chargé(e) de facturation maintenance assure la gestion et le suivi de la facturation des contrats de maintenance et des prestations associées.

Il/Elle veille à la fiabilité des données contractuelles et tarifaires, au respect des échéances de facturation et à la bonne transmission des éléments nécessaires à la comptabilisation et au suivi du chiffre d'affaires.

Il/Elle contribue à l'amélioration continue des processus de facturation et à la qualité de la relation avec les clients et les interlocuteurs internes.

Principales responsabilités

Gestion de la facturation des contrats de maintenance

  • Assurer la facturation périodique des contrats de maintenance selon les conditions contractuelles (annuelle, trimestrielle, mensuelle).
  • Vérifier les éléments contractuels et les conditions tarifaires avant émission des factures.
  • Créer et mettre à jour les données de facturation dans les outils de gestion.
  • Établir les factures initiales, les renouvellements et les éventuelles factures complémentaires.
  • Gérer les avoirs et les régularisations nécessaires.
  • Veiller au respect des délais de paiement par les clients et participer à la relance en cas d’impayé en lien direct avec le client pour une transformation efficace de la facturation en trésorerie.
  • Veiller au respect du calendrier de facturation et à l'exhaustivité des factures émises.


Suivi administratif et fiabilisation des données

  • Assurer le suivi administratif des contrats de maintenance en lien avec les équipes concernées.
  • Contrôler la cohérence entre les contrats signés, les données clients et les éléments de facturation.
  • Identifier et régulariser les éventuelles anomalies ou incohérences.
  • Assurer la mise à jour des informations nécessaires à la facturation : coordonnées clients, conditions tarifaires, dates de début et de fin, modalités de renouvellement.
  • Assurer le classement et l'archivage des documents justificatifs.


Coordination avec les équipes internes et les clients

  • Collaborer étroitement avec les équipes commerciales, ADV, support et finance afin de collecter et fiabiliser les informations nécessaires à la facturation.
  • Suivre les demandes et réclamations clients relatives aux factures.
  • Assurer les échanges avec les clients pour résoudre les éventuels litiges ou questions de facturation.
  • Alerter les interlocuteurs concernés en cas de contrats non facturés, d'informations manquantes ou de retards.


Reporting et amélioration continue

  • Participer au suivi des indicateurs de facturation : volumes facturés, factures en attente, anomalies, retards.
  • Contribuer au suivi du chiffre d'affaires récurrent lié aux contrats de maintenance.
  • Proposer des améliorations visant à sécuriser et fluidifier le processus de facturation.
  • Participer à l'évolution des procédures et des outils de gestion administrative et financière.


Profil recherché

Formation et expérience

  • Formation Bac +2 minimum en gestion, comptabilité, administration des ventes ou gestion financière.
  • Expérience de 2 à 3 ans minimum sur un poste similaire, idéalement dans un environnement B2B.
  • Une expérience en facturation récurrente, gestion de contrats ou facturation de prestations de services constitue un atout.


Compétences techniques

  • Bonne maîtrise des processus de facturation et des règles de gestion associées.
  • Bonne maîtrise d'Excel et des outils bureautiques.
  • Aisance avec les logiciels de gestion commerciale, ERP ou outils de facturation.
  • Connaissance des principes comptables et des règles de TVA.
  • La connaissance de la facturation de contrats de maintenance ou de services récurrents est un plus.


4. Qualités personnelles

  • Rigueur et sens du détail.
  • Organisation et capacité à gérer des échéances récurrentes.
  • Autonomie et sens des responsabilités.
  • Esprit d'analyse et capacité à identifier les anomalies.
